title_en: China Acrobatic Troupe Co., Ltd. v. Zhang Shuo Acrobatic Troupe of Sangyuan Town, Wuqiao County, et al. — dispute over copyright ownership and infringement
keywords_en: civil; copyright infringement dispute; first instance; basic people's court; Beijing Municipality; Hebei Province; Guangdong Province; Henan Province; legal person; natural person; Copyright Law; determination of originality of acrobatic works; distinction between public domain and originality; scope of protection of acrobatic works; liability of internet service providers; plagiarism of acrobatic programs; copyright registration; infringement via network dissemination; performance in Spring Festival Gala; copyright; copyright infringement; infringement dispute
full_text_en:
China Acrobatic Troupe Co., Ltd. v. Wuqiao County Sangyuan Town Zhang Shuo Acrobatic Troupe, et al. — Dispute over Copyright Ownership and Infringement

[Case Gist]

Where the main form of expression consists of acrobatic movements, with personalized arrangements, choices, and designs in the衔接 and choreography of movements, and which possesses a certain degree of artistic expression and originality, it may be recognized as an acrobatic art work under the Copyright Law. Simple combinations and repetitions of routine acrobatic movements in the public domain, due to insufficient originality, do not fall within the scope of protection of the Copyright Law.

Where a work mainly consists of acrobatic movement design but incorporates certain dance movement designs, it may be protected as a whole as an acrobatic art work. For the accompanying music, costumes, and stage design in an acrobatic program, it shall be determined whether they can constitute other types of works such as musical works or artistic works based on their specific form of expression, and then whether they should be independently protected.

Plaintiff: China Acrobatic Troupe Co., Ltd., domiciled at Jian'an Street, Beijing Economic-Technological Development Area, Beijing.
Legal Representative: Qi Hong, Chairperson of the Company.

Defendant: Wuqiao County Sangyuan Town Zhang Shuo Acrobatic Troupe, business premises at Sangyuan Town, Wuqiao County, Cangzhou City, Hebei Province.
Operator: Zhang Shuo, male, born on October 18, 1989, Han ethnicity, residing in Wuqiao County, Cangzhou City, Hebei Province.

Defendant: Shenzhen Tencent Computer Systems Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 1, Science and Technology Middle Road, Maling Community, Yuehai Street, Nanshan District, Shenzhen City, Guangdong Province.
Legal Representative: Ma Huateng, Chairperson of the Company.

Defendant: Jian'an District Radio and Television Station, Xuchang City, domiciled at Xinxu Road, Xuchang City, Henan Province.
Legal Representative: Wang Zongzhao, Director of the Station.

The plaintiff, China Acrobatic Troupe Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "China Acrobatic Troupe"), filed a lawsuit with the Xicheng District People's Court of Beijing against the defendants, Wuqiao County Sangyuan Town Zhang Shuo Acrobatic Troupe (hereinafter "Zhang Shuo Acrobatic Troupe"), Shenzhen Tencent Computer Systems Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Tencent Company"), and Jian'an District Radio and Television Station, Xuchang City (hereinafter "Jian'an District TV Station"), concerning a dispute over copyright ownership and infringement.

Plaintiff's Allegations: China Acrobatic Troupe claimed to be the copyright owner of the acrobatic program "Qiao Hua Dan - Collective Diabolo" (《俏花旦-集体空竹》). The defendant Zhang Shuo Acrobatic Troupe's acrobatic program "Qiao Hua Dan" (《俏花旦》) performed at the 2017 Xuchang County Spring Festival Gala copied the movement combinations, background music, and actor costumes of "Qiao Hua Dan - Collective Diabolo," constituting copyright infringement. The video of the "Qiao Hua Dan" program was available for streaming on the website with the domain name V.QQ.COM and on the WeChat public account "Image of Xuchang" (映像许昌). The defendant Jian'an District TV Station produced and broadcast the program video, and the defendant Tencent Company failed to fulfill its duty of review for the dissemination of the video on its website, also constituting copyright infringement. Accordingly, the plaintiff requested that Zhang Shuo Acrobatic Troupe, Tencent Company, and Jian'an District TV Station cease the infringement and compensate for losses.

Defendant Zhang Shuo Acrobatic Troupe's Defense: The plaintiff's "Qiao Hua Dan - Collective Diabolo" copied the "Wang's Tianqiao Acrobatics" (王氏天桥杂技). The defendant had never seen the plaintiff's program and had only watched the "Qiao Hua Dan Diabolo" (《俏花旦抖空竹》) performed by the Cangzhou Acrobatic Troupe. The defendant rehearsed based on the Cangzhou Acrobatic Troupe's program. Diabolo is a traditional folk culture and must not be registered by any entity or individual. Before the Copyright Law was enacted in 2010, there was no legal provision allowing acrobatics to be registered for copyright. Acrobatics is a special industry requiring years of training. It would be obviously unreasonable to find infringement when an acrobat who has practiced a program for over ten years has it preemptively registered by someone else.

Defendant Tencent Company's Defense: First, the basis of the plaintiff's rights and whether the program constitutes an acrobatic work under the Copyright Law are difficult to determine. Second, the WeChat public account service and Tencent Video service provide information storage space services to account owners and registered users, allowing them to provide various types of information to the public through information networks. Tencent Company did not make any modifications or deletions to the involved video uploaded. According to Tencent Company's backend records, the involved video had been deleted by the uploader before Tencent Company received the plaintiff's complaint. As a network service provider, Tencent Company did not know and had no reasonable grounds to know about the infringement of the involved video. Even if the involved video constituted infringement, Tencent Company should not bear liability for compensation.

Defendant Jian'an District TV Station's Defense: The recording of the program was legally authorized. There is a certain similarity between the defendant Zhang Shuo Acrobatic Troupe's program and the plaintiff's program, including identical background music and similar names. However, the TV station was unaware of this at the time of recording and was not at fault, so it should not bear liability for compensation. According to the relevant provisions of China's Copyright Law, the TV station's actions did not constitute infringement. If the program constituted infringement, it was caused by Zhang Shuo Acrobatic Troupe's program imitating China Acrobatic Troupe, and the responsibility should be borne by Zhang Shuo Acrobatic Troupe. The TV station is willing to cooperate with China Acrobatic Troupe to eliminate the impact, but the involved infringing program has already been removed from the involved networks. Therefore, the plaintiff's claim for cessation of infringement lacks factual basis. In summary, the TV station requested the court to reject all of China Acrobatic Troupe's claims.

Facts Found by the First Instance (Xicheng District People's Court of Beijing):

The Copyright Registration Certificate No. 00008667 states: The documents submitted by the applicant, China Acrobatic Troupe, conform to the requirements. For the acrobatic work "Qiao Hua Dan - Collective Diabolo (French Version)," which was created in 2004 (choreographers He Xiaobin and Zhang Ruijing, composer Du Ming, costume Song Li) and first performed in February 2005, the applicant, as the copyright owner, enjoys copyright (except for the right of attribution of authors) in accordance with the law. Registration No.: 2007-L-08667, Date of Issuance: August 31, 2007.

China Acrobatic Troupe (Party A) entered into an agreement titled "China Acrobatic Troupe Co., Ltd. Agreement on Copyright Ownership of Choreographers for Acrobatic Works 'Teng Yun - Thirteen Person Bowl Balancing' and 'Qiao Hua Dan - Collective Diabolo'" with He Xiaobin and Zhang Ruijing (Party B), stipulating that Party A holds the copyright in the commissioned works, and all property rights in the copyright belong to Party A. As to the moral rights in the copyright of the above commissioned works, Party B enjoys the right of attribution, and Party B agrees that Party A exercises the other rights.

China Acrobatic Troupe (Party A) entered into an agreement titled "China Acrobatic Troupe Co., Ltd. Agreement on Copyright Ownership of Music Creation for Acrobatic Work 'Qiao Hua Dan - Collective Diabolo'" with Du Ming (Party B), stipulating that Party A holds the copyright in the commissioned work, and all property rights in the copyright belong to Party A. As to the moral rights in the copyright of the above commissioned work, Party B enjoys the right of attribution, and Party B agrees that Party A exercises the other rights.

China Acrobatic Troupe (Party A) entered into a "Contract for the Production of Costumes for Acrobatic Works 'Qiao Hua Dan - Collective Diabolo' and 'Sheng Dou · Di Quan'" with Beijing Jinwu Costume Production Center (Party B), stipulating that Party A commissions Party B to complete the costume production for the 2013 Monaco competition program "Qiao Hua Dan - Collective Diabolo," and Party A holds the copyright in the finished costumes produced by Party B.

The acrobatic program "Qiao Hua Dan - Collective Diabolo" has won the following awards: the "Yellow Crane Gold Award" at the 6th China Wuhan Optics Valley International Acrobatic Art Festival in 2004; the highest award, the "Presidential Prize of the French Republic," at the "26th International Festival de l'Art du Cirque de Demain de la France" in 2005; the first prize in the "Audience's Favorite Spring Festival Gala Program (Drama and Folk Art Category)" at the 2007 CCTV Spring Festival Gala; the 2010 World Intellectual Property Organization Gold Award (China) for Works; and the "Golden Clown Award" at the 37th Monte Carlo International Circus Festival in Monaco in 2013.

On January 17, 2017, Xuchang County TV Station (later merged into the defendant Jian'an District TV Station) held a gala titled "The 2017 Xuchang County Spring Festival Gala: A Happy Year of Ten Thousand Lights." For this purpose, Xuchang County TV Station (Party A) and the defendant Zhang Shuo Acrobatic Troupe (Party B) signed a "Commercial Performance Contract," stipulating that Xuchang County TV Station invited Zhang Shuo Acrobatic Troupe to perform the acrobatic program "Qiao Hua Dan." The performance time was January 17, 2017. Party A paid Party B a total performance fee of RMB 17,000 (after tax). The performance venue was Xuchang, Henan.

The Notarial Certificate (2017) Jing Xin De Nei Jing Zheng Zi No. 00041, issued by Beijing Xinde Notary Public Office on February 20, 2017, shows that by logging into WeChat on a mobile phone and searching for "Image of Xuchang" in the "Public Accounts," a public account named "Image of Xuchang" can be found, with the filing entity being Xuchang County TV Station. In the historical messages of this public account, "The 2017 Xuchang County Spring Festival Gala (Part 2)" can be found. Upon entering the interface, the corresponding video can be played. At the point "43:06/54:50" in the video, the alleged infringing program marked "Dance Acrobatics 'Qiao Hua Dan' performed by China Wuqiao Acrobatic Art Center" can be seen.

The Notarial Certificate (2017) Jing Xin De Nei Jing Zheng Zi No. 00042, issued by Beijing Xinde Notary Public Office on February 20, 2017, shows that by entering the web address "V.QQ.COM" in the address bar of a computer browser and entering "2017 Xuchang County Spring Festival Gala" in the search bar, clicking on "The 2017 Xuchang County Spring Festival Gala (Part 1)" and "The 2017 Xuchang County Spring Festival Gala (Part 2)," the corresponding videos can be played normally. The video headers bear the words "Xuchang TV Station January 25, 2017" and "2017 Xuchang County Spring Festival Gala: A Happy Year of Ten Thousand Lights." The "Tencent Video" icon appears in the upper right corner of the video playback frame.

The defendant Jian'an District TV Station admitted that the above videos were uploaded by it but have since been deleted, and the "Image of Xuchang" public account has also been closed.

The total duration of the plaintiff China Acrobatic Troupe's "Qiao Hua Dan - Collective Diabolo" French version video is 14 minutes and 12 seconds, with the acrobatic program performance lasting 9 minutes and 48 seconds. The defendant Zhang Shuo Acrobatic Troupe's "Qiao Hua Dan" appears in the "2017 Xuchang County Spring Festival Gala (Part 2)" video from 9 minutes and 2 seconds to 14 minutes and 9 seconds, with a duration of 5 minutes and 8 seconds. Comparing China Acrobatic Troupe's "Qiao Hua Dan - Collective Diabolo" French version with Zhang Shuo Acrobatic Troupe's "Qiao Hua Dan," the following similarities were found: both use the same background music; in terms of specific movements, both are based on the technical characteristics of "diabolo" itself; the image is styled as the "Dan" role in Chinese opera; the stage movements incorporate elements such as the Chinese opera "running in circles" (跑圆场); in the "entrance" segment, after excluding the differences in the stage environment, the core expressions of the performance segments of both are similar; in some iconic collective movements forming a连贯 series of actions, the expressions are identical or highly similar. Additionally, the stage forms of the two programs are different, and there are some differences in specific acrobatic movements.

Comparing the performance costumes in the plaintiff China Acrobatic Troupe's "Qiao Hua Dan - Collective Diabolo" Monaco version video with those in the defendant Zhang Shuo Acrobatic Troupe's "Qiao Hua Dan" program, the colors and shapes are highly similar. Specifically, both have a collar design around the neck, pink lotus flowers on the short skirts, and a pattern of alternating blue and white lines on the short skirts. The difference lies in the fact that in China Acrobatic Troupe's Monaco version, the blue color on the upper chest of the costume transitions into a heart shape, while in Zhang Shuo Acrobatic Troupe's "Qiao Hua Dan" program, the entire upper chest area above the bust is blue.

Additionally, the plaintiff China Acrobatic Troupe provided a "Power of Attorney Agreement," special VAT invoices, and travel expense receipts. The invoices indicate that China Acrobatic Troupe paid attorney fees of RMB 15,000 and notarization fees of RMB 6,000.

Opinion of the First Instance (Xicheng District People's Court of Beijing):

Whether an acrobatic program constitutes an acrobatic art work must first satisfy the general constitutive elements for works: it must be an intellectual achievement in the fields of literature, art, or science and technology; it must be an expression in a certain tangible form, rather than a mere idea; and the content of the expression must possess originality. According to the above definition and constitutive elements of acrobatic art works, only original acrobatic physical movements and techniques that possess a certain degree of artistic expression can constitute an acrobatic art work within the meaning of the Copyright Law (2010 Amendment). The "competitive nature" expressed in acrobatic art works is not an essential element of acrobatic art works. The venue, place, equipment, performance mode, etc., of acrobatic performances are also not within the scope of protection of the Copyright Law.

In this case, the main expressive content of the acrobatic program "Qiao Hua Dan - Collective Diabolo" for which the plaintiff China Acrobatic Troupe claims rights is "collective diabolo play." The穿插 and integrated opera movements and dance movements are inseparable from the technical movements of "diabolo play," forming an integrated artistic expression. The stage artistic image of "Qiao Hua Dan playing diabolo" is emotionally impactful, the acrobatic movements are vivid and lively, and it establishes a specific connection with the choreographer and the copyright owner, constituting a work within the meaning of the Copyright Law. This work is distinct from the existing folk skill of "diabolo play" and should be protected under China's Copyright Law. Based on the evidence submitted by the parties, it can be determined that China Acrobatic Troupe enjoys the copyright in the acrobatic art work "Qiao Hua Dan - Collective Diabolo," except for the right of attribution of the respective authors.

Comparing the "Qiao Hua Dan" performed by the defendant Zhang Shuo Acrobatic Troupe with "Qiao Hua Dan - Collective Diabolo," the opening performance segments are highly similar. The衔接 between dance movements and diabolo movements, and parts of the rhythmic arrangement of dance steps are identical. The designs for some performance segments and the positioning choreography of performers on the performance stage are similar. In terms of duration, the similarities account for approximately one-third. The court of first instance determined that Zhang Shuo Acrobatic Troupe's copying of parts of the content of "Qiao Hua Dan - Collective Diabolo" constituted infringement, and its involved performance behavior infringed upon the performance right enjoyed by the plaintiff China Acrobatic Troupe. Furthermore, the background music of "Qiao Hua Dan" and "Qiao Hua Dan - Collective Diabolo" is essentially the same, and the costumes are highly similar, also constituting infringement. The defendant Jian'an District TV Station, by producing a gala program containing "Qiao Hua Dan" and broadcasting it via radio signals, and by disseminating the program video to the public through an information network, infringed upon the broadcasting right and the right of communication through information networks enjoyed by China Acrobatic Troupe. The defendant Tencent Company, as a network service provider, had no fault regarding the alleged infringing act and should not bear liability for compensation.

Accordingly, the Xicheng District People's Court of Beijing, in accordance with Articles 8, 12, and 13 of the Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China; Articles 1, 3, 10, 17, 47(5), 48(1), and 49 of the Copyright Law of the People's Republic of China; Articles 4 and 27 of the Regulations for the Implementation of the Copyright Law of the People's Republic of China; Articles 25 and 26 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Disputes over Copyright; Articles 14 and 22 of the Regulations on the Protection of the Right to Communicate Works through Information Networks; and Article 64(1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on June 25, 2019:

1. The defendant Wuqiao County Sangyuan Town Zhang Shuo Acrobatic Troupe shall cease the involved infringing acts against the plaintiff China Acrobatic Troupe Co., Ltd.'s "Qiao Hua Dan - Collective Diabolo" within the validity period of this judgment;
2. The defendant Wuqiao County Sangyuan Town Zhang Shuo Acrobatic Troupe shall, within 30 days of this judgment taking effect, publish a statement in the People's Court Daily to eliminate the effects of its involved infringing acts (the published content must be reviewed by the court; in case of default, the court will, upon the application of the plaintiff China Acrobatic Troupe Co., Ltd., publish the main content of this judgment in relevant media, with costs borne by the defendant Wuqiao County Sangyuan Town Zhang Shuo Acrobatic Troupe);
3. The defendant Jian'an District Radio and Television Station, Xuchang City, shall, within 30 days of this judgment taking effect, publish a statement in the People's Court Daily to eliminate the effects of its involved infringing acts (the published content must be reviewed by the court; in case of default, the court will, upon the application of the plaintiff China Acrobatic Troupe Co., Ltd., publish the main content of this judgment in relevant media, with costs borne by the defendant Jian'an District Radio and Television Station, Xuchang City);
4. The defendant Wuqiao County Sangyuan Town Zhang Shuo Acrobatic Troupe shall, within seven days of this judgment taking effect, compensate the plaintiff China Acrobatic Troupe Co., Ltd. for economic losses in the amount of RMB 40,000, and the defendant Jian'an District Radio and Television Station, Xuchang City, shall bear joint and several liability for RMB 10,000 of that amount;
5. The defendant Jian'an District Radio and Television Station, Xuchang City, shall, within seven days of this judgment taking effect, compensate the plaintiff China Acrobatic Troupe Co., Ltd. for economic losses in the amount of RMB 10,000;
6. The defendant Wuqiao County Sangyuan Town Zhang Shuo Acrobatic Troupe and the defendant Jian'an District Radio and Television Station, Xuchang City, shall, within seven days of this judgment taking effect, compensate the plaintiff China Acrobatic Troupe Co., Ltd. for reasonable expenses (including attorney fees, notarization fees, and travel expenses) in the amount of RMB 28,239;
7. Reject the other claims of the plaintiff China Acrobatic Troupe Co., Ltd.

Zhang Shuo Acrobatic Troupe, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, appealed to the Beijing Intellectual Property Court. Zhang Shuo Acrobatic Troupe's Grounds of Appeal: The appellee China Acrobatic Troupe stated in its complaint that the involved acrobatic program "Qiao Hua Dan - Collective Diabolo" originated from "Wang's Tianqiao Acrobatics." This shows that "Qiao Hua Dan - Collective Diabolo" lacks originality. According to the provisions of the Copyright Law, only acrobatic art works with artistry and originality can be protected objects of the Copyright Law. Furthermore, the duration of China Acrobatic Troupe's "Qiao Hua Dan - Collective Diabolo" program is 9 minutes and 48 seconds, while the duration of Zhang Shuo Acrobatic Troupe's "Qiao Hua Dan" performance is 5 minutes and 8 seconds. Although both use the same background music, the acrobatic movements are different and the meanings conveyed to the audience are different. The Copyright Law does not clearly define which elements of imitation or to what extent imitation constitutes infringement for acrobatic art. What is not prohibited by law is permitted. Therefore, Zhang Shuo Acrobatic Troupe's performance of "Qiao Hua Dan" does not constitute infringement and does not require assumption of tort liability.

The Appellee China Acrobatic Troupe argued: The judgment of first instance found clear facts and correctly applied the law. China Acrobatic Troupe agrees with the conclusion of the first instance judgment. The appellant Zhang Shuo Acrobatic Troupe's performance of "Qiao Hua Dan" infringed upon China Acrobatic Troupe's performance right in the acrobatic work "Qiao Hua Dan - Collective Diabolo." The appellant's grounds of appeal lack factual and legal basis and should be dismissed.

The Appellee Tencent Company argued: Tencent Company is merely a network service provider. It did not edit, organize, or recommend the involved video. The appellee China Acrobatic Troupe did not send a takedown notice to Tencent Company. Tencent Company has fulfilled its corresponding obligations and should not bear liability.

The Appellee Jian'an District TV Station argued: It agrees with the appellant Zhang Shuo Acrobatic Troupe's opinion that the appellee China Acrobatic Troupe's "Qiao Hua Dan - Collective Diabolo" program does not constitute a work protected by the Copyright Law, and that Zhang Shuo Acrobatic Troupe's "Qiao Hua Dan" program does not constitute substantial similarity with it. Jian'an District TV Station's broadcast of the program did not infringe China Acrobatic Troupe's copyright. Regarding the background music, Jian'an District TV Station has legal authorization and should not bear tort liability. Regarding compensation for losses, even if infringement is established, the amount of compensation should be calculated based on the fees Zhang Shuo Acrobatic Troupe received from Jian'an District TV Station, rather than being determined by discretion.

The Beijing Intellectual Property Court, after second instance trial, confirmed the facts found in the first instance.

Opinion of the Second Instance (Beijing Intellectual Property Court):

I. Whether the French Version of "Qiao Hua Dan - Collective Diabolo" for which the appellee China Acrobatic Troupe claims rights constitutes an acrobatic art work under the Copyright Law

China’s Copyright Law lists acrobatic art works alongside musical, dramatic, quyi, and dance works as a separate category of works, indicating that acrobatic art works constitute an independent type of work distinct from dramatic works, dance works, etc. Acrobatic art works include specific types such as acrobatics, magic, and circus, and are “works expressed through physical movements and skills.” The content of such works is not the skill itself.

(1) Separate protection of acrobatic art works

In affording separate protection to acrobatic art works, attention must be paid to the differences between acrobatic art works and similar works, the most typical being dance works. Both dance works and acrobatic art works are works primarily expressed through human movements, but there are still certain differences between them. The movements in acrobatic art works mainly emphasize technical skill, and are achieved through highly difficult body or prop control that ordinary people cannot easily master; the general public can recognize that such movements primarily belong to specific categories of acrobatics. The movements in dance works are often rhythmic body language used to convey emotions and shape characters, usually performed with music. Compared to the former’s emphasis on skill and difficulty, dance works focus more on emotional expression and even character portrayal.

It should be noted that, at the present stage, many acrobatic works incorporate dance elements in movement design and choreography, including integrating dance movements into acrobatic movements and introducing dance movements between connecting acrobatic movements. In such circumstances, forcibly dividing the continuous movements into fragmented dance movements and acrobatic movements, thereby eliminating the dance elements, will greatly diminish the aesthetic quality of the original work, and the separated movement choreography can hardly be protected independently as dance or acrobatic works. Therefore, works that primarily consist of acrobatic movement design but also incorporate certain dance movement design can still be protected as acrobatic art works.

Furthermore, during actual performances, acrobatic art works often include accompanying music, specialized costumes for performers, and corresponding stage art design in addition to movements. However, the legislation has clearly defined that acrobatic art works are expressed through physical movements and skills, and are not composite works like audiovisual works that can be protected as a whole encompassing music works, fine art works, etc. Therefore, even if the aforementioned accompanying music constitutes a music work and the costumes and stage art design constitute fine art works, they are not part of the acrobatic art work and cannot be incorporated into the content of the acrobatic art work for protection; instead, they should be independently protected as different types of works.

(2) Primary factor of originality in acrobatic art works: choreography and design of movements

Acrobatic art works take movements as their basic element, and skills are also exhibited through specific movements. However, acrobatic art works do not protect the skill itself, nor do they generally protect specific individual movements; rather, they protect the choreography and design of continuous movements. The carrier is similar to dance notation in dance works. Of course, the choreography and design of movements protected by acrobatic art works must possess artistry and reach a certain level of originality. If it is merely a simple combination or repetition of conventional acrobatic movements in the public domain, the originality is insufficient and should not be protected under copyright law.

(3) Whether the French version of the work *Qiao Hua Dan - Collective Diabolo* in this case constitutes an acrobatic art work

In this case, viewing the content of the French version of *Qiao Hua Dan - Collective Diabolo*, its many “diabolo” movements are additionally infused with movements and even facial expression designs that incorporate elements from traditional Chinese opera and dance. For example, the overall movement of performing a large-stride single-leg lift step and a three-step footwork while simultaneously shaking the diabolo with both hands left and right or up and down. Additionally, there are individualized arrangements in the specific positioning, connecting movements, and choreography, so that the corresponding continuous movements convey artistic beauty while demonstrating superb physical skills. On this basis, the appellant, Zhang Shuo Acrobatic Troupe, failed to provide evidence to the court proving that the above designs and choreography primarily come from the public domain or constitute limited expression. Therefore, the court does not accept its aforementioned assertion. The court holds that the choreography and design of physical movements in the French version of *Qiao Hua Dan - Collective Diabolo* reflect the creator’s individualized choices, constitute an expression with originality, and qualify as an acrobatic art work under the Copyright Law.

II. Whether the first instance court’s determination of substantial similarity was correct

Regarding the comparison between the French version of *Qiao Hua Dan - Collective Diabolo* as an acrobatic art work and *Qiao Hua Dan* performed by the appellant Zhang Shuo Acrobatic Troupe, the court holds that copying does not require verbatim reproduction of the original without any alteration. In the determination of infringement of the performance right, if it is found that the content performed without authorization constitutes substantial similarity to a relatively complete part of the original work’s original expression, and there is a possibility of the alleged infringer having had access to the original work, and independent creation is excluded, infringement can likewise be established. The choreography and design of movements in *Qiao Hua Dan*, including the positioning and movement connections in the opening part as well as the iconic collective movements that appear multiple times, are substantially similar to the corresponding content of the French version of *Qiao Hua Dan - Collective Diabolo*. The above content constitutes part of the original expression of the French version of *Qiao Hua Dan - Collective Diabolo*. Therefore, the first instance court’s finding that Zhang Shuo Acrobatic Troupe committed plagiarism and infringed the performance right is correct. The aforementioned grounds of Zhang Shuo Acrobatic Troupe lack legal basis, and the court does not accept them.

In conclusion, pursuant to Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People’s Republic of China, the Beijing Intellectual Property Court rendered the following judgment on November 1, 2021:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.
